newsitem.title: UK: UK election race far tighter than polls show - Blair.
newsitem.headline: UK election race far tighter than polls show - Blair.

text.p: British opposition leader Tony Blair has poured cold water on opinion polls showing his Labour Party is cruising towards an overwhelming victory in the May 1 election.

"The election is not yet won. I discount the polls. I do not believe them," Blair said in an interview with the left-leaning political weekly New Statesman published on Thursday."I think it is going to be a far tighter and harder race than they suggest."
The Conservatives have been in power since 1979, having won four successive elections.
But earlier this week two opinion polls showed Labour 25 and 28 points ahead of the Conservatives, enough to give them an overall majority of 200-240 seats in a parliament of 659 members.
But Blair said: "They (the Conservatives) are not going to hand over the keys to Downing Street (the prime minister's residence) without a fight."
Labour needs a 4.3 percent swing from the Conservatives compared with the 1992 election if it is to win an overall majority of seats in the new parliament.
On the opinion poll figures, it has achieved close to four times that.

Blair has long been urging his party not to take victory for granted. In a final speech to his MPs on Wednesday before parliament disperses for the election, he told them: "Complacency is the enemy of success."
